speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) with brachial plexus involvement.

Based on your history of weight loss, smoking, alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use, combined with progressive right arm weakness and sensory loss, this clinical picture strongly suggests a lung malignancy at the apex invading the brachial plexus. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, MRI_Brachial_Plexus. REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT_With_Contrast.
